layman_headline: Both open trades are in profit and approaching targets — time to let winners run, not chase new entries.
layman_explanation: Bitcoin just surged past $68,000 on positive regulatory news from the White House, dragging the entire market higher. Our Solana position is up 8.1% and within striking distance of its $85 profit target. Chainlink is up 5.9% and also closing in on its exit. The swing candidates on the watchlist are either overbought (BTW at RSI 93), stablecoins, or gold-backed tokens that don't fit a swing trade profile. Rather than force a new entry in this already-extended bounce, we should focus on managing our winning positions.
layman_action: Hold current positions. Consider taking profit on SOL if it hits $85 and LINK if it reaches $10.90. Do not open new trades until the market pulls back and offers a fresh setup.
expert_reasoning: The market is experiencing a sharp relief rally driven by regulatory tailwinds (Clarity Act, CFTC/Hyperliquid news) and macro support (Treasury buybacks). SOL is up 8.6% on the week with $3.2B in 24h volume — approaching the $85 exit target set at entry. LINK has rallied 15.4% in 7 days and is nearing its $10.90 target. The swing candidates list is poor quality this cycle: BTW has an RSI of 92.7 (extreme overbought), gold tokens XAUT/PAXG are defensive plays unsuited for swing trading, MON lacks technical data, and the rest are stablecoins. With Fear & Greed improving from 34.9 weekly average to 46, and BTC dominance at 57% still suppressing altcoin beta, the risk-reward of chasing new entries here is unfavorable. Better to manage existing winners and wait for a pullback to re-enter.

context_banner: Relief rally in progress with both positions approaching profit targets — discipline means taking gains, not adding risk.
